title: World Cinema Radar — the podcast, Tuesday 3 November 2026

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Hello, and welcome to World Cinema Radar, the podcast. I'm {A}, and it's Tuesday the third of November.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: And I'm {B}. <chuckle> The weekend is over, the Halloween candy is gone, and the news is a little quieter today. But there is still plenty to talk about.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: We start with the American box office. A documentary has just beaten a superhero-adjacent film at the top of the chart. That's not a sentence you hear often.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Then we visit Tokyo, where the film festival is in its final days. After that, a bit of opera: the Liceu in Barcelona has set a date for a new digital release.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: We'll also run through the calendar for the week, and then our picks. Everything is in the written edition, with sources and dates.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Right. <short pause> Let's get going.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: A small note before we start. We read everything for this edition on Sunday night and this morning, and where sources disagree, we say so.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Which happens today, a couple of times. <chuckle> You'll hear it.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Today the theme is simple. Fewer stories, checked properly. That is better than a long list with doubts.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: So, the box office. The weekend of the thirtieth of October to the first of November, in the United States and Canada. And number one is a documentary.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: A documentary? |Really?| Really. It's called You Can See Everything, it comes from A24, and it made ten point six million dollars in its third weekend.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Ten point six million. And the total is now sixty-three point eight million. For a documentary, that is huge.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: It's huge. And here's the detail I love. According to the Rotten Tomatoes report, it's the first non-concert documentary to reach number one since Fahrenheit nine eleven. That was in two thousand four.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Twenty-two years. <laugh> So Halloween had no real monster to offer, and the winner is a documentary.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: A quiet weekend, yes. The report itself calls it slow. And a caveat: these are estimates. Different box office sources did not fully agree on who finished first, so the numbers can still change.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Good point. Because second place is very close. Clayface made ten point four million.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Ten point four, which is a fall of fifty-seven percent from its opening weekend. After ten days it has forty-four million.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Which is not a disaster, but it isn't a superhero triumph either. We talked about its opening last week and the word was disappointing, more or less.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Right. Then third place is Wildwood, the animated film from Laika. Seven point five million, and twenty-five point nine million in total.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: I like that. Laika is a stop-motion studio, so every frame is a lot of work. Good to see people showing up.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Then fourth is Wicker. A Sundance title, from the distributor Black Bear. It was widened to more than two thousand three hundred theatres, and it made four point one million. Thirteen point two so far.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Thirteen million for a Sundance title is a decent run. <short pause> Though we only have the money today, so let's not read too much into it.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Agreed. Four point one million this weekend, thirteen point two in total, and that's all the report tells us.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Fair. Then there is a little curiosity: BTS's concert film Arirang made three million dollars, in one single night in cinemas.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: One night! That tells you something about fan power.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: It does. And let's remember, this is all America. None of this tells us how these films will do in Spain, or even when they open here.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Exactly. And one last line from the report: next weekend, the holiday season starts with the animated film The Cat in the Hat.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: So the quiet weekend is over. <short pause> A documentary on top, a slow Halloween. I think that's a nice little story for a Tuesday.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Let me say why this matters for us. This is a Tuesday news item, but it says something about audiences. People are choosing real stories over franchises this month.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Careful, {A}. <chuckle> One weekend is not a trend. But it is a pleasant surprise, and the report treats it that way too.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Fair. I'll say it differently: it's a good reminder that the chart is not always led by the biggest marketing budget.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: And the Clayface number is a good example. Forty-four million after ten days is not nothing, but a fall of fifty-seven percent is steep for a film of that size.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Steep, yes. And remember, these are the numbers for the United States and Canada only.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Which is why we always add the line: this tells us nothing about Spain. A film can be a hit in America and arrive here months later, or never.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Or the other way round. We've seen both. <laugh>

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: So, to sum up this segment: the documentary is first, Clayface second, Wildwood third, Wicker fourth, and a concert film in the top six after a single night.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: That's the whole top of the chart, and it is not what anyone predicted a month ago.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: One more angle on this documentary. Nobody expected a documentary to play like this, and that is what makes the chart interesting this week.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: True. In a normal month the top five is full of sequels. Here we have a documentary, a stop-motion film, a Sundance title and a concert film.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Plus Clayface. <chuckle> Let's not forget Clayface.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: We never forget Clayface. Okay, moving on.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Now, Tokyo. The thirty-ninth Tokyo International Film Festival runs from the twenty-sixth of October to the fourth of November. So we are in the final stretch.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: And it's big. According to Japan Travel, it shows two hundred and four films from a hundred and twelve countries and regions.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: A hundred and twelve. <gasp> That is a lot of passports.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: And the theme this year is Connecting. Cinema as a bridge to the world. There are also director Q and As, masterclasses and public workshops, mostly around Hibiya, Yurakucho, Marunouchi and Ginza.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Fifteen films are in competition for the Tokyo Grand Prix. The jury president is Rolf de Heer, the Australian director.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: With the actress Makiko Watanabe and the producer Alex Lo. A nice, small jury.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: The festival opened with Sukiyaki, directed by Zeze Takahisa. And the closing film is Colony, a Korean zombie action horror from Yeon Sang-ho.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Now, that is a good closing film for us. Horror, big action, Korean cinema. That fits the profile very well.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: It does. And in the middle, the centrepiece is Godzilla Minus Zero.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Which also opens in Spain this Friday, the sixth of November, according to Sensacine. That is one of the ones we will mention in the calendar.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Now, here is the honest part. We could not find the date of the awards ceremony. None of the sources we read says it.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: So we will wait. <short pause> The festival ends on the fourth, so I would expect the verdict then, but that is an expectation, not a fact.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Right. We will report the official winners as soon as we have them.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: And for listeners, the thing to notice is the mix. Asian auteur cinema and genre films in the very same week. That's what makes Tokyo fun.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: I want to go back to the numbers for a second. Two hundred and four films in ten days. Nobody sees all of them.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Nobody. That is why the competition of fifteen films is a good way in. Fifteen titles are for the grand prize, and the rest is a giant buffet.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: A buffet, I like that. <giggle> And the public workshops and masterclasses are part of it too, so it's not only for people with accreditation.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Right. The festival is also spread over four central neighbourhoods, so you can walk from one cinema to the next.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Which sounds lovely, honestly. And for us, the two big Asian genre titles at the edges of the programme, Sukiyaki at the opening and Colony at the close, are both worth keeping on the radar.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Sukiyaki is described as a music drama by Zeze Takahisa. And Colony is the zombie one. Quite a range.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Big range. And the jury has an Australian president, an actress from Japan and a producer. That is a mix of viewpoints, which I think is healthy.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: One more thing. Godzilla Minus Zero is the centrepiece in Tokyo, and in Spain it opens this Friday. So a festival film is also a cinema release here. We don't see that overlap every day.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: No, we don't. And we'll keep an eye on the awards.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Time for our daily opera and theatre corner. This one is from Barcelona. The Gran Teatre del Liceu has a date for the digital release of I Capuleti e i Montecchi, by Vincenzo Bellini.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: That's the Romeo and Juliet story, but in Bellini's version. The date is the twenty-second of November, on LiceuOPERA Plus, their streaming platform.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: And the price is interesting. Subscribers of the theatre get it at a special price of forty-five euros.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Forty-five euros for subscribers. And ninety euros for everyone else.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Ninety. <sigh> Opera is not cheap, even from the sofa.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: No. But it's a full production from a big house, so I understand the logic. Still, I'd like to see what I'm paying for.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: And that's the catch. The page does not say who is singing, who directs the staging, or when it was recorded.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: So we can't treat it as a full filmed performance yet. We will not recommend it as one until we have those details. That is our rule.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: The platform also lists the rest of the digital season. La bohème on the thirty-first of January. La fanciulla del West in April. Jenufa in June. And The Magic Flute in July.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: A nice mix. And we talked about the Liceu's Aida, from the twenty-fifth of October, a few days ago, if you want something to watch right now.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Good tip. <chuckle> Opera on demand, for a rainy Tuesday.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Let me play devil's advocate on the price. Forty-five euros for subscribers is a special price. What does a subscriber get beyond that?

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: From the page, the platform is included in the fixed subscription at that price. The page also talks about multicamera viewing and new camera setups, in general terms, for the platform.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: General terms. So nothing specific about this Bellini, again.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Exactly. That is why we call it announced and not recommended. We have a date, a platform, a price. We lack the rest.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: I do like the idea that a Spanish opera house is building a whole digital season. Five more titles after this one. That's a real catalogue.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: It is. And Bellini fits our taste for classic repertoire and for the Romeo and Juliet story, which is always a good theatre theme.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Once the cast is announced, we'll tell you. <short pause> Until then, circle the twenty-second in your calendar.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Let's do the calendar. Tuesday the third, nothing new on our list.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Quiet. Wednesday the fourth, the Tokyo festival ends.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Thursday the fifth, a screening of Golden Boy by National Theatre Live, in a cinema in Colchester, in the United Kingdom. There is a second screening on the thirteenth.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: That is a UK date, so it doesn't help us in Spain. But it's good to know it is out there.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Then the big day. Friday the sixth, in Spain, Godzilla Minus Zero opens, and so does Sacamantecas, along with other titles, according to Sensacine.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: And on Netflix, the same day, Possible Love, the new film from Lee Chang-dong.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Later in the month. Wednesday the eleventh, El cuerpo on Netflix. Sunday the twenty-second, the Liceu stream we just talked about.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Friday the twenty-seventh: Sanguine. Now, careful here. Sensacine says the twenty-seventh, but Cinemania says the sixth.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: So the date needs checking. <short pause> We will say more when we know.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: And Monday the thirtieth, the Gotham Awards. And remember, dates from other countries don't apply to Spain.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: A word about how we read these dates. Spain first, other countries separately. A date from Korea, Japan or the United States does not count for us here.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: That's our rule for every release, and it protects us from the classic mistake: assuming that a film opens here the same day it opens elsewhere.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Which is why the Colchester screening is listed as UK only. Fun for people who live there, but not for us.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: And that Friday the sixth is the busy one. Godzilla Minus Zero, Sacamantecas, other releases, and Possible Love on Netflix.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: If you only have one evening, it is a choice between the cinema and the sofa.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: A cinema night for Godzilla, a sofa night for Lee Chang-dong. <chuckle> Sounds like a plan.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Our picks. First, Possible Love. Lee Chang-dong, eight years after Burning. Our affinity score is four out of five, with medium confidence.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: A reminder: that score is not a critics' score. It is just our guess at how well it fits the profile. And we haven't seen the film. We only know it from reports.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Second, Sanguine. French body horror that won at Sitges. Four out of five, medium confidence. And as we said, the Spanish date is the sixth or the twenty-seventh.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Third, the Liceu's Capuleti e i Montecchi. Three out of five, low confidence, because the cast and recording details are missing.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: So that's three suggestions for a short edition.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: A short edition is better than a long one full of rumours. <chuckle> I'll take that.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: We should explain what affinity means, for new listeners. It's a number from zero to five that says how well a title fits the reader's taste. Horror, historical cinema, smart comedy, auteur films, stage and opera.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: And confidence says how much we really know. High, medium or low. Today none of the three is high, because we haven't seen any of them.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: That honesty is the whole point. We only write what we can source.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: So Possible Love is the safest bet. Sanguine is the one for horror fans, and the Liceu is the one for patient opera lovers.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: The idea of the day: a small documentary can beat the big names, and a quiet news day is still a good one if the facts are solid.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: And two things to remember: Possible Love and the Spanish releases on Friday. Thanks for listening.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: See you tomorrow on the Radar.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: See you tomorrow.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: And one more thing before we go. If a date matters to you, check the written edition. Each report has its sources listed, and the dates are separated by country.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Good advice. Especially for Sanguine, where two sources give two different days.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Exactly. Enjoy the week, and watch something good.
